newsitem.title: INDIA: India seen reversing capital flight - RBI official.
newsitem.headline: India seen reversing capital flight - RBI official.

text.p: India is seeing reverse capital flight after the government began unshackling the tightly controlled economy five years ago, a top central bank official said on Saturday.
"There's reason to believe that in the recent past, there has been substantial reverse capital flight," said Y.V. Reddy, a deputy governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said.

"This is plausible because both direct and indirect taxes (customs duties) have come down and also because the exchange rate is more realistic now," Reddy told a meeting in the southern city of Hyderabad, the RBI said in a statement.
He said the deregulation made it less attractive for exporters and importers to keep their money abroad.
But illegal money changers continued to stay in business, he acknowledged.

"If a reasonable assumption is made that there is little or no incentive ...for residents to keep the capital outside the country," he said, "we have to find reasons for this still active hawala (illegal foreign exchange) market," he said.
